annotations.title: Put a business in the directory

description: For a business's own AI: put the business in the directory with its doors (MCP, A2A, OpenAPI, an API, UCP, ACP, a platform's door) and its facts (name, category, where, languages), and agree to the listing terms (/bot#terms). When its proof is not in place yet, the answer gives a challenge (a file or DNS record on its domain, its inbox manifest, a key's signature, or a code mailed to its domain) and the next call proves it. Mail, phone, forms and web pages are never doors. Free, and the order cannot be bought. Not listed: adult services, gambling, weapons, tobacco, cannabis and vaping, payday loans, bail bonds.

agree.description: The business agrees to be listed by the network's published rules (GET /v1/ranking) and listing terms.

alternate_names.description: Other names the business goes by; a name longer than the network keeps is dropped (the reference network keeps 60 characters and 4 words at most).

category.description: What the business is: one category, and at most two more.

alternates.description: Up to two more categories, as primary takes them.

primary.description: A place category id (GET /v1/categories?group=…) or a group slug.

claim_token.description: Given by a successful register_business: proof again for 90 days, for this listing only.

description.description: One line on what it does; the first line is at most 160.

domain.description: The business's own website domain. A business without a website is not supported yet.

doors.description: Its doors for AI agents; each counts only after this network's crawler has checked it.

kinds.description: Of ask, quote, book, order: what it answers.

protocol.description: What it speaks, for type "other": like beckn or graphql.

rate_limit.description: Requests a day this door takes, 1 to 20; it only lowers the network's own.

terms_url.description: The door's terms of use, https.

type.description: inbox, mcp, a2a, openapi, api, ucp, acp, nlweb, webhook, other, or platform:<name>. Mail, phone, messaging, forms and web pages are human channels and never doors.

url.description: https, with no user in it.

closures.description: Closed dates, each from and to, both included.

timezone.description: A tz database zone, like Europe/Paris.

weekly.description: Days mon to sun, each with [open, close] pairs in HH:MM; a day left out is closed.

languages.description: Language tags, like pt or fr-CA.

proof.description: Proof the domain is its own, answering the challenge a call without proof gets.

challenge_id.description: The challenge's id, as the answer gave it; none for code.

code.description: code: the 8 digits sent to that address.

email.description: code: an address at exactly the business's own domain (not a subdomain), typed by the owner; never a public mail or internet provider's domain.

method.description: Which of the challenge's ways was used.

want_inbox.description: true: once the domain is proved, the answer says how its owner sets up an agent inbox.

where.description: A storefront needs an address or geo, a service area its radius or countries, online its ships_to.

geo.description: The storefront's point on a map.

kind.description: Each way it serves customers: storefront, service_area, online.

service_area.description: Where it goes to its customers: a radius in km, or countries.

ships_to.description: Countries it delivers to, as two-letter ISO 3166 codes, or * for all.

name: register_business

outputSchema.description: Every field is described in this tool's outputSchema at https://network.surfingdog.ai/.well-known/mcp/server-card.json.

card.description: The listing as it stands now, as search_businesses gives each business.
